body.p: Many years ago, three strong men lived. They lived when the Evenki first came to be. Those strong men lived well, they did not argue, did not fight. When one of them said something, they did not argue; when they did something, they did not do it on their own, they did it together, talking to one another, agreeing. All Evenki knew them. There were no other strong men like them there. When they went to hunt, they left behind their friends. They build their hous out of larchs. They attached three larchs at the top like a golomo, they lived there. Each day they got to know strong men. Many years go by, they heard that there was a strong man with the Yakuts, one stronger than them. They could not find him at all. That Yakut had been informed about them and about where the three men lived. He started to look for them. The strong Yakut man searched for three years, in the fourth year he learned more about them. That Yakut looked for(?) the strong men, he travelled with four reindeer sleds day and night to get to them. He took the reindeer in order to be able to run away from them quickly once he had won. At last, he reached them. When he reached them, he saw: larchs are attached at the top making a house. The Yakut was very scared: "What have I come to?" He tied the reindeer [to something], he entered their [house]. Three people lived in the house. Their house is very very good. They were rich, there was a lot of food. After entering, he greeted them. They were very good, kind-hearted. They gave him to eat. They told each other [stories] while night came. He spent the night with them. In the morning they got up early, drank tea a couple of times. While they were sitting, one of the three strong men said to the visiting Yakut: "Friend, let us compare strength, show us what you are made of." The Yakut agreed. The four of them went outside. First the strong man who had asked fought [with him]. That one who had asked was the oldest of them. He fought with the strong Yakut man. The Yakut threw him around a little. The middle brother fought [with him]. Again he was thrown around by the Yakut. Then only the youngest brother was left. This one was stronger than the older brothers. He fought with the Yakut. He lifted that Yakut up, threw him away. Since then they believe that they are the strongest of all. The Yakut travelled home quickly after losing. The older brothers of the winner were angry to have lost against the Yakut. They started to follow him in order to kill him. They were in a small hollow near his house. In autumn, the Yakut would hunt elks in the hollow. The oldest of the brothers took a shotgun and snuck closer to the Yakut. When he had approached, he shot him, killed that one, he went home. From that day on, there was noone stronger than them.
